scope: Full daily Power Stack research refresh across all established categories and tracked regions, including US, Hong Kong/China and Malaysia. Research/data only; no site code, UI, scoring logic, automation logic or backend architecture changes.

promotions.name: Rockwell Automation
promotions.reason: Profitable first-wave automation exposure with fiscal Q3 2026 organic sales +10%, 22.3% enterprise operating margin, raised FY2026 guidance, and explicit strength in semiconductor, data-centre and warehouse automation.

promotions.name: CBH Engineering Holding Berhad
promotions.reason: Differentiated Malaysian 275kV substation/data-centre grid exposure. Q2 2026 revenue and net profit more than doubled year over year and a new RM246m Johor award extends visibility, though concentration and ACE Market risk cap conviction.

existingUniverseReview.summary: Every tracked category and the existing visible/supplemental research universe were re-screened against current macro, company and sector evidence. No existing conviction change cleared the bar today. The most important change is not a single-stock downgrade but a sharper split between strong physical demand and hostile financing/input-cost conditions.
notableCompanyReads: NBIS: financing risk increased after a $5bn convertible issue, potentially $5.75bn, on top of about $12bn total convertible debt; Q2 sales still rose fivefold to $582m, so keep the growth thesis but do not increase conviction until capital efficiency improves.

MRNA/MRK: positive Phase 3 melanoma vaccine result remains strategically important, but full hazard ratios, overall-survival data, manufacturing turnaround and commercial economics are still pending; no further score change after the August 20 addition.
GEV/PWR/ETN/HUBB/POWL: demand thesis remains supported; valuation sensitivity is higher because long yields rebounded.
XOM/CVX/CNOOC/WMB/KMI/LNG: energy-security and gas-infrastructure theses remain supported; refiners have the cleaner near-term product-tightness signal.
VLO/MPC: tactical setup strengthened further because U.S. diesel cracks exceeded $100/bbl and global refining outages remain severe.
BWXT/CEG/1816.HK/LEU/CCJ: nuclear/fuel thesis unchanged and supported by China buildout and energy-security policy; speculative developers remain rate/valuation sensitive.
SYM/2590.HK/CGNX/TER/9880.HK: hierarchy unchanged; commercial fixed automation remains ahead of humanoids.
TNB/YTLPOWR/SCGBHD/MNHLDG/SunCon/NationGate: Malaysia data-centre demand remains real, but the best relative setup is still grid/electrical picks-and-shovels rather than pure AI-hardware beta.

categoryChanges.read: Still the strongest structural category. Physical demand remains excellent, but 10Y/30Y yields around 4.7%/5.25% restore a meaningful duration/valuation headwind. Prefer backlog-rich equipment, T&D and regulated-grid names.

Demand remains strong, but financing risk is becoming more visible. Nebius's outsized convertible financing is a reminder that capacity growth can destroy equity value if capital intensity outruns returns. Prefer electrical, cooling, water and construction bottlenecks with real margins over balance-sheet-heavy compute capacity.

Structural thesis unchanged. China approvals/commissioning and Western fuel-security needs remain supportive. No new name displaced BWXT/CEG/1816.HK on operating quality or CCJ/LEU on fuel-chain relevance.

Refined-product scarcity is now more important than crude alone. Diesel cracks above $100/bbl and large Middle East/Russian refinery outages strengthen VLO/MPC tactical economics, while Brent around $93 remains geopolitically supported but demand-sensitive.

Copper's structural case strengthened but near-term pricing is distorted by a severe LME squeeze. Treat the squeeze as confirmation of a thin physical buffer, not as a permanent earnings run-rate. BHP remains the preferred diversified expression.

No adoption-wave reorder. First-wave fixed/warehouse/factory automation gained further evidence through Rockwell's results, while Unitree itself still frames broad embodied intelligence as years away. ROK clears the quality bar as a new research candidate.

China left 1Y/5Y LPRs at 3.00%/3.50%. Weak domestic demand persists, but fiscal infrastructure execution remains the policy preference. This supports power/grid/nuclear more than broad cyclical consumption.

The data-centre electrical buildout continues to show up in real contract awards. CBHB now clears the research bar as a direct 275kV substation/grid-connection candidate, but concentration and liquidity keep it below the core-quality global grid names.

macro.rates: Long-end Treasury relief faded; 30Y returned near 5.247% and 10Y near 4.70% on August 20.
macro.oil: Brent was near $93.49; refining/product shortages remain the more acute inflation signal.
macro.creditVolatility: Broad credit remains more resilient than the weakest-borrower tail, but high sovereign yields and capex financing keep duration risk elevated.
macro.chinaRates: 1Y LPR 3.00%, 5Y LPR 3.50%, unchanged for a 15th month.
macro.copper: LME cash copper briefly reached about $14,912/t during a flash squeeze; physical inventories remain unusually tight and geographically distorted.

ism.keyRead: Manufacturing demand, production and backlog remain strong while customers' inventories are too low; services demand is firm but Employment contracted and Prices accelerated. Electrical components, semiconductors, memory, copper, switchgear, transformers and wire/cable remain the most Power Stack-relevant bottlenecks.
ism.rawSubmissionCaveat: ISM publishes aggregate diffusion data and selected respondent comments, not confidential/raw individual survey submissions.

researchGaps: Get a fresh valuation/technical pass on the highest-conviction US grid names after the renewed long-yield selloff; demand is strong enough that valuation is now the main gating variable.
Add a deeper China/HK motion-control/reducer/servo screen around listed suppliers rather than chasing humanoid OEMs after the World Robot Conference.
Validate CBHB customer concentration, cash conversion and working-capital quality before moving above 7.9.
Track NBIS capex-to-revenue conversion and dilution after the latest convertible issue; the demand signal is strong but capital efficiency is now the core risk.
Wait for full Moderna/Merck Phase 3 melanoma disclosure before another conviction change.
Monitor refinery repair timelines and product inventories; the current refining trade can reverse quickly if Hormuz/refinery capacity normalises.
